subject: general
question:
Fill in the blanks:

In Indian classical music notation, a swara with a dot above the letter (e.g., S) represents the [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/efbb4cd1cdb04e3d55ec812b33b49b9c823e135e641878fdc8e5762164dc7a84.png] saptak.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Taar Saptak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Indian Classical Music**, the term **Saptak** refers to a set of seven musical notes (Swaras): **Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, and Ni**.
 
• According to the **Bhatkhande Music Notation System**, which is widely used in **Hindustani Classical Music**, symbols are used to indicate different registers or octaves.
 
• A **dot placed above** a letter (e.g., Ṡ, Ṙ, Ġ) signifies the **Taar Saptak**, also known as the **Upper Octave**. These notes have a sound frequency that is exactly **double** that of the corresponding notes in the middle register.
 
• The **Taar Saptak** register is used to denote higher-pitched sounds and is essential for expanding the melodic range of a **Raga** during performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mandra Saptak** (Lower Octave):

 
 
• Represented by placing a **dot below** the swara letter (e.g., Ṣ, Ṛ, G̣). This indicates a deep, base register with half the frequency of the **Madhya Saptak**.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Saptak** (Middle Octave):
 
 
• This is the **normal register** where a musician mostly sings or plays. In notation, these notes are written **without any dots** above or below (e.g., S, R, G, M, P, D, N).
 
 
 
• **Shuddha Saptak**:
 
 
• This refers to a scale consisting entirely of **Shuddha (Natural)** swaras. In **Hindustani Classical Music**, the notes of **Bilawal Thaat** are considered the standard **Shuddha Saptak**.
